method: Installed-data synthetic one-vehicle static detection and response. Actual five-sphere PE descriptors, wheel-extended aggregate, shape pool/cache, parsed-index spatial registration, initial terrain/model candidate builders, full terrain and placed-model sphere queries, sphere-list wrappers, default real static-contact merge, queue, dispatcher, contact storage, signed-counter-bounded candidate regeneration and frame completion. Three declared profiles at sampled covered terrain cells and up to three upward model faces per pack: normal offsets26/14/26 units and normal speeds-16/-4/+16 units per frame. All contact classes/times are computed from geometry, never supplied. Unit mass/inverse mass, zero restitution, recovered inertia, identity rotation with rotation integration disabled, recovered drive-class row, explicit pool order, zeroed scratch, selection counter0, ordinary time scaling, nearest-even conversion and active tag5. Candidate geometry lists are retained from the initial broad phase throughout response; no cache rebuild, wheel forces, gravity integration, attachment execution, captured runtime state, original process execution or complete race equivalence. Object/class1 destruction callbacks return false; class2 callback is inert but native class2 damping is preserved. Class16 removal requests from static-contact merger rejection (including zero penetration projection) are recorded through an explicit inert lifecycle callback: the synthetic body remains registered for frame-completion validation, so this does not reconstruct object removal or native post-removal behavior. Sampled complete retained-x86 terrain checks compare actual corpus geometry and scratch state.
